message.content:
The sea doesn’t have one fixed color—it looks different depending on a few factors:

| Factor | Typical Appearance |
|--------|--------------------|
| **Depth** | Shallow water (a few meters) often looks turquoise or green because the water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange) and reflects shorter ones (blue, green). |
| **Sunlight angle** | At noon, the sea can appear a deep blue; at sunrise/sunset it may look pinkish or orange. |
| **Algae or plankton** | High concentrations can give the water a greenish tint. |
| **Distance** | The farther you look, the bluer the sea tends to appear because the water scatters blue light more efficiently. |
| **Reflection** | The sky’s color, clouds, and surrounding land can influence how the sea looks. |

So, while “blue” is the most common description, the sea can range from turquoise to green to even a pale gray or brownish hue under certain conditions.
